title: Epidemiological Statistics
curriculum_locator: Stat H-304 Epidemiological Statistics; University of Dhaka four-year B.S. Honours Statistics curriculum, starting session 2023–2024

units.title: Foundations of Epidemiology, Surveillance & Measures of Disease Frequency
scope: Historical origins of epidemiologic thinking: John Snow and the Broad Street cholera pump, Ignaz Semmelweis, William Farr, and causal paradigms
Target populations, cohorts (open, closed, fixed), and person-time accounting; incidence proportion (cumulative incidence) vs incidence density (rate)
Prevalence (point and period prevalence) and the fundamental steady-state dynamic equilibrium identity P = (I * D) / (1 + I * D)
Direct and indirect age-standardization: Standardized Mortality Ratios (SMR), comparative mortality figures, and the choice of standard populations
Public health surveillance architectures: passive vs active surveillance, syndromic reporting, sentinel systems, and data completeness

units.title: Measures of Association & Public Health Impact: Risk Ratios, Odds Ratios & Attributable Fractions
scope: Risk Ratio (Relative Risk) and Rate Ratio: mathematical definitions, geometric interpretation, and asymptotic log-scale sampling distributions
Odds Ratio (cross-product ratio): mathematical properties, invariance under retrospective sampling, and the rare disease assumption approximation
Attributable Risk (Risk Difference) and Attributable Fraction among the Exposed (etiologic fraction): biological and policy interpretations
Population Attributable Risk (PAR) and Population Attributable Fraction (PAF, Levin's and Miettinen's formulas) for public health resource prioritization
Asymptotic confidence intervals via the multivariate Delta method: Woolf's logit method for odds ratios and score-based intervals
Number Needed to Treat (NNT) and Number Needed to Harm (NNH): mathematical definitions, reciprocal properties, and clinical utility

units.title: Observational & Experimental Study Designs: Cohort, Case-Control, Cross-Sectional & Clinical Trials
scope: Taxonomy of epidemiologic study architectures: observational vs experimental, longitudinal vs cross-sectional, prospective vs retrospective
Prospective and retrospective cohort studies: participant recruitment, baseline exposure ascertainment, person-time tracking, and loss to follow-up
Case-control study designs: case definition, control selection paradigms (density sampling, cumulative sampling, case-cohort), and recall bias
Cross-sectional surveys and ecological studies: measurement of concurrent status, prevalence odds ratios, and the ecological fallacy
Randomized Controlled Trials (RCTs): parallel group, cross-over, factorial designs, blinding, intention-to-treat (ITT) vs per-protocol analysis
Matching in study designs: individual (pair) matching vs frequency matching, overmatching hazards, and efficiency tradeoffs

units.title: Methodological Validity: Confounding, Selection Bias, Information Bias & Effect Modification
scope: Internal vs external validity in epidemiologic investigations; taxonomy of systematic errors vs random variation
Confounding: classical epidemiologic criteria, causal DAG definitions (backdoor paths), colliders, and M-bias structures
Stratification analysis: Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel (CMH) pooled odds ratio and risk ratio estimators, and variance estimators
Assessment of effect measure modification (statistical interaction): additive vs multiplicative scale interactions, Synergy index (S)
Tests of homogeneity: Breslow-Day test, Tarone's adjusted test, and Woolf's chi-square test across stratified 2x2 tables
Information bias (misclassification): differential vs non-differential misclassification of exposure or disease, and bias direction toward/away from null

units.title: Multivariable Regression in Epidemiology: Logistic, Conditional Logistic, Log-Binomial & Poisson Models
scope: Binary logistic regression: logit link, parameter interpretation as adjusted odds ratios, maximum likelihood estimation via Newton-Raphson
Matched case-control data and conditional logistic regression: profile likelihood eliminating nuisance stratum intercepts, 1:1 and 1:M matching
Direct estimation of adjusted relative risks: log-binomial regression models, convergence difficulties, and modified Poisson regression with robust sandwich variance
Poisson regression for incidence rates: log link with log(person-time) offset, rate ratio interpretations, and goodness-of-fit deviance tests
Overdispersion in count data: negative binomial regression model, dispersion parameter estimation, and zero-inflated models
Confounder selection strategies: change-in-estimate criterion, directed acyclic graph guided covariate adjustment, and avoiding collider stratification

units.title: Screening, Diagnostic Testing & Receiver Operating Characteristic (ROC) Analysis
scope: Principles of secondary prevention and Wilson-Jungner screening criteria; screening vs diagnostic testing
Fundamental 2x2 diagnostic performance metrics: sensitivity, specificity, false positive rate, false negative rate
Predictive values: Positive Predictive Value (PPV) and Negative Predictive Value (NPV), and their dependence on disease prevalence
Bayesian formulation of clinical diagnosis: prior odds, Positive Likelihood Ratio (LR+), Negative Likelihood Ratio (LR-), and posterior odds
Receiver Operating Characteristic (ROC) curves: continuous diagnostic biomarkers, cutoff variation, and parametric vs non-parametric estimation
Area Under the Curve (AUC / c-statistic): probabilistic interpretation as Wilcoxon-Mann-Whitney statistic, Youden's J statistic, and cutoff optimization

units.title: Infectious Disease Epidemiology: Transmission Dynamics, Compartmental Models & Outbreak Investigation
scope: Epidemic curves and outbreak investigation: point-source, propagated, and continuous common-source outbreaks; secondary attack rates
Kermack-McKendrick compartmental models: deterministic SIR and SEIR systems of ordinary differential equations
The Basic Reproduction Number R_0: biological definition, derivation via the Next-Generation Matrix approach, and threshold phenomenon
Effective reproduction number R_t: real-time estimation from serial interval distributions and daily case notification counts (Wallinga-Lipsitch method)
The Herd Immunity Threshold (HIT = 1 - 1/R_0) and critical vaccination fraction required for disease elimination
Epidemic final size equation: transcendental relation linking R_0 and the ultimate proportion of the population infected (R_infinity)

units.title: Survival Analysis in Epidemiology & Causal Inference Frameworks
scope: Time-to-event data structures: right censoring, left truncation (delayed entry), survival function S(t), hazard function h(t), and cumulative hazard H(t)
Nonparametric survival estimation: Kaplan-Meier product-limit estimator, Greenwood's variance formula, and log-rank test for group comparison
Cox Proportional Hazards model: semi-parametric specification h(t | x) = h_0(t) exp(beta^T x), partial likelihood, and hazard ratio interpretation
Diagnostics for proportional hazards: Schoenfeld residuals, log-cumulative hazard plots, and time-varying covariates
The Counterfactual and Potential Outcomes framework (Neyman-Rubin causal model): consistency, exchangeability, and positivity assumptions
Marginal structural models and Inverse Probability of Treatment Weighting (IPTW) for time-varying confounding and causal hazard ratios
